title: Chemistry: FCI Wavefunction to QubitWaveFunction
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

UnitaryHack: Would only recommend this task if pre-exposure to quantum chemistry exists. 
To run the example code:

```bash
pip install tequila-basic
pip install pyscf
```

Currently exact ground states of chemistry Hamiltonians can only be obtained by direct diagonalization

```python
geometry = "Be 0.0 0.0 0.0\nH 0.0 0.0 -1.0\nH 0.0 0.0 1.0"
mol = tq.Molecule(geometry=geometry, basis_set="sto-3g")

H = mol.make_hamiltonian()
v,vv = numpy.linalg.eigh(H.to_matrix())

# ground state wavefunction
wfn = tq.QubitWaveFunction(vv[:,0]) 

```

where sparse matrices/solvers can help a bit, but also run out of steam soon. 

With a full-CI solver (FCI), we can treat larger systems (as we don't need to resolve the whole Fock space), but currently tequila only supports energies (via pyscf)
```
fci_energy = mol.compute_energy("fci")
```

It would be great to have access to the wavefunction as well.
PySCF can compute FCI wavefunctions, but they will not be given back in qubit format, but in a special quantum chemistry format called alpha and beta strings. Roughly this corresponds to Determinants that can be mapped to Jordan-Wigner encoded qubit wavefunctions. 


**Describe the solution you'd like**
Basically this function in tequila (ideally implemented into [pyscf backend](https://github.com/tequilahub/tequila/blob/master/src/tequila/quantumchemistry/pyscf_interface.py) (see for example `compute_fci` to see how the fci energy is currently calculated)
```python

# standalone or integrated into the pyscf interface
def compute_fci(self, get_wfn=True):
    .....
    
    # type of wfn: tq.QubitWaveFunction
    wfn = convert_pyscf_fci_wfn_to_qubit_wfn(....)    

    if get_wfn:  
        return energy, wfn
        
```


**Additional context**
To test the method, one can do the following:
```python
geometry = "Be 0.0 0.0 0.0\nH 0.0 0.0 -1.0\nH 0.0 0.0 1.0"
mol = tq.Molecule(geometry=geometry, basis_set="sto-3g")

H = mol.make_hamiltonian()
v,vv = numpy.linalg.eigh(H.to_matrix())

# ground state wavefunction
wfn = tq.QubitWaveFunction(vv[:,0]) 
energy = v[0]

fci_energy, fci_wfn = FUNCTION_TO_IMPLEMENT

fidelity = abs(fci_wfn.inner(wfn))**2
assert numpy.isclose(fidelity, 1.0)
assert numpy.isclose(fci_energy, energy)
```


The data format in pyscf is most likely alpha/beta strings. These lecture notes from [Sherrill](https://vergil.chemistry.gatech.edu/static/content/ci.pdf) are probably quite helpful.
